title: Whataburger rises to No. 20 on list of top fast-food chains in the nation - NewsBreak
text:
By Lily O'Neill ,
2 days ago Whataburger announced two new restaurant prototypes earlier this year. Its new A-frame designs are a callback to founder Harmon Dobson’s 1960s vision. (Rendering courtesy of Whataburger) Whataburger is among the top 20 fast-food chains in the nation.
Restaurant industry publication QSR released its 2026 annual report ranking the quick-service sector’s top 50 performers based on systemwide sales, average-unit volumes and growth in 2025.
The San Antonio-based chain moved up two spots this year, coming in at No. 20. McDonald’s, Starbucks and Chick-fil-A earned the top three spots in QSR’s top 50 ranking.
“This recognition reflects the incredible work our Family Members do every day to deliver the quality, hospitality, and consistency our Guests have come to expect from Whataburger,” Jessica Reicher, Whataburger’s executive vice president and chief operating officer, said in a statement. “We’re proud of the progress we’ve made, and we’re excited to build on that momentum by continuing to deliver our best Guest experience and earn our Guests’ loyalty with every visit.”
Whataburger beat out Arby’s, Jersey Mike’s and Jack in the Box. Among the burger chains on the list, Whataburger ranked No. 6 based on sales. It had systemwide sales of $4.31 billion, according to the report.
“Whataburger is leaning into nostalgia, family occasions, and menu innovation as the Texas-born burger chain continues expanding into new markets across the U.S.,” the report reads.
READ MORE: Meet the executive chef shaping Whataburger’s menu innovations
Last year, Whataburger added 76 more units for a total of 1,161, the majority of which are corporate-owned.
When Chicago-based BDT Capital Partners acquired a majority stake in Whataburger from the founding Dobson family in 2019, the private equity firm announced plans to aggressively expand. Soon after, Whataburger began franchising for the first time in nearly two decades, adding stores in new cities and existing markets while pushing into new states, including Colorado, Kansas and Missouri.
In addition to expanding into new regions, Whataburger has continued to invest in the customer experience while embracing its origins.
Whataburger this year relaunched its Kids Whatameal experience, introducing a refreshed look and adding a surprise toy to every meal. The homegrown brand also announced two new restaurant prototypes , one of which will pay homage to its original A-frame design. It plans to debut the first two in Texas next year and develop more in its North Carolina, South Carolina, Florida, Arizona and Georgia markets.
RELATED: Whataburger going retro with new restaurant prototype
The Texas institution’s menu innovation starts with corporate executive chef James Sanchez and his team of product developers, who spend 18 months to two years developing a new product or revising an existing one. Whataburger’s recent limited-time menu items include the Hot Honey Crisp Whatachick’n Sandwich, the Strawberry Hibiscus Whatafresher and the return of the Bacon Steakhouse Double and Banana Pudding Shake.
Alongside its growth, Whataburger has brought in more executive leaders with national experience.
At the end of the month, former Torchy’s Tacos and Taco Bell exec Ryan Moore will join as chief financial officer . Last year, Debbie Stroud, a former Starbucks and McDonald’s exec, became CEO , while Reicher, the former president of Arby’s, filled the chief operations officer role . And in 2024, Todd Huetinck — a veteran of Carl’s Jr. and Hardee’s parent company, CKE Restaurants Holdings Inc. — became Wh ataburger’s chief supply chain officer.
